title: Grove's capital requirements distinguish markets within a single Instance, so the Instance is not the finest unit of risk control
content:
A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.3.7.1.1.2.5.2 assigns two different capital requirements inside one Instance: the schedule from 3% to 0.65% "applies to the **approved spUSDG/USDG market**," while "any allocation to the **syrupUSDG/USDG market, which is not approved**, is subject to a 100% CRR."

Everything else about the Instance is undifferentiated. There is one inflow RateLimitID, one 50,000,000 USDG deposit limit, one maxExchangeRate, one token. Grove deposits USDG into a Morpho vault, and the vault allocates across markets — so the market-level distinction is downstream of every on-chain control the Instance defines.

That breaks the framing that holds through most of the Grove Liquidity Layer, where the Instance is the atom of both authorization and enforcement. Here authorization is finer-grained than enforcement: the Atlas expresses a preference between markets that no RateLimitID can implement, because the allocation decision belongs to the vault curator, not to Grove.

The consequence is that this Instance's real risk profile depends on a party whose choices Grove does not control and whose actions the Instance's controls cannot bound. The vault could rotate its allocation between the approved and unapproved markets without any Grove limit registering a change.

That is precisely why the differentiation had to be expressed as a **capital requirement** rather than a limit — a CRR is computed from where the exposure ends up, so it can reach a distinction that a transaction-time control cannot. Where an allocation is intermediated by a curator, capital charges are the only instrument that follows the money to its destination.
description: The Grove x Steakhouse USDG Instance carries a 3%-to-0.65% CRR for the approved spUSDG/USDG market and a 100% CRR for the unapproved syrupUSDG/USDG market under one set of rate limits.
